title: A quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes is an open immersion into an affine scheme finite over the base (Stacks 03GU)
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that $X$ and $Y$ are affine and $f$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then there exist an affine scheme $Z$, an open immersion $j:Y\to Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and a finite morphism $\pi:Z\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] with $f=\pi\circ j$. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU, which is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure) reformulated for schemes: for $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $R\to S$ of finite type and quasi-finite, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S''$ for a finite $R$-subalgebra $S''$ of the integral closure of $R$ in $S$.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU (lemma-quasi-finite-affine), line 15230, and its proof (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB, algebra.tex line 30906)

proof.text: *Affine charts.* Put $R=\mathcal O_X(X)$, $S=\mathcal O_Y(Y)$ and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be the ring map induced by $f$ (the map $f^\sharp_X:\mathcal O_X(X)\to\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}(X))=\mathcal O_Y(Y)$; the restriction map is the identity). As $X$ and $Y$ are affine, $X\subseteq X$ and $Y\subseteq Y$ are affine opens with $f(Y)\subseteq X$, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] gives open immersions $\iota_X:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ and $\iota_Y:\operatorname{Spec}S\to Y$ with images $X$ and $Y$, and for every $y\in Y$ a prime $\mathfrak q_y\subset S$ with $\iota_Y(\mathfrak q_y)=y$. An open immersion whose image is all of the target is an isomorphism: by [def-weil-open-immersion] it induces an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $(Y,\mathcal O_Y|_Y)=Y$. So $\iota_X$, $\iota_Y$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-scheme], $\mathfrak q_y=\iota_Y^{-1}(y)$, and every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ is $\mathfrak q_y$ for $y=\iota_Y(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square] (with $U=Y$, $V=X$, whose induced ring map is $\varphi$) we have $\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=f\circ\iota_Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that is, $f=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi\circ\iota_Y^{-1}$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03GU, lines 15249-15250 ('Algebra, Lemma 00QB reformulated in the language of schemes'): the passage from the affine schemes X, Y to the ring map R -> S

proof.text: *The ring map is of finite type and quasi-finite.* By [pqf-def-quasifinite] (3), $f$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (finite type is locally of finite type and quasi-compact), and every $y\in Y$ is an isolated point of its fibre. With $x=f(y)$ and $Y_x=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ the fibre, whose first projection $p:Y_x\to Y$ is a homeomorphism onto the subspace $f^{-1}(x)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], there is a unique point $\xi\in Y_x$ with $p(\xi)=y$, and $\{\xi\}$ is open in $Y_x$ (by that homeomorphism, $y$ isolated in $f^{-1}(x)$ and $\xi$ isolated in $Y_x$ say the same). Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime and $y=\iota_Y(\mathfrak q)$, so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_y$ by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] to the morphism $f:Y\to X$, which is locally of finite type, the point $y$, and the affine opens $U=Y\ni y$, $V=X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, $\mathcal O_Y(U)=S$, $\mathcal O_X(V)=R$, induced ring map $\varphi$ and prime $\mathfrak q_y=\mathfrak q$ corresponding to $y$: it gives that $\varphi$ is of finite type and that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. As $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, $\varphi$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime ideal of $S$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03GU, lines 15249-15250: the hypothesis 'R -> S of finite type and quasi-finite' of Algebra 00QB obtained from 'f quasi-finite' (Definition Tag 01TD, definition-quasi-finite)

proof.text: *Zariski's main theorem.* By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-ring-map-integral-closure-open] (3) (Algebra 00QB), applied to $\varphi$ by step 2, there is a subring $S''$ of the integral closure $S'$ of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], containing $\varphi(R)$ and finitely generated as an $R$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], such that the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}e:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}S''$ induced by the inclusion $e:S''\to S$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\psi:R\to S''$, $r\mapsto\varphi(r)$, be the corestriction of $\varphi$ (defined since $\varphi(R)\subseteq S''$). Then $\varphi=e\circ\psi$, and $\psi$ is finite: $S''$ is a finitely generated $R$-module via $\psi$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure), line 30905, part (3), as invoked in the proof of Morphisms Lemma Tag 03GU

proof.text: *The factorization.* Put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S''$, an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-pc-scheme], $j=\operatorname{Spec}e\circ\iota_Y^{-1}:Y\to Z$ and $\pi=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi:Z\to X$. The morphism $j$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]: $\iota_Y^{-1}$ is an isomorphism (step 1) and $\operatorname{Spec}e$ an open immersion (step 3), and precomposing with an isomorphism keeps $j$ a homeomorphism onto the same open subset $\operatorname{Spec}e(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ of $Z$ and keeps $j^{-1}\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal O_Y$ an isomorphism (it is the isomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}e$ transported along the isomorphism $\iota_Y$). By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and step 1, $\pi\circ j=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi\circ\operatorname{Spec}e\circ\iota_Y^{-1}=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e\circ\psi)\circ\iota_Y^{-1}=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi\circ\iota_Y^{-1}=f$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU, the diagram of the statement (lines 15237-15244) and the proof, lines 15249-15250

proof.text: *$\pi$ is finite.* Since $\psi$ is finite (step 3), $\operatorname{Spec}\psi:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a finite morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite]. The commutative square with top $\mathrm{id}_Z$, left $\pi:Z\to X$, right $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ and bottom $\iota_X^{-1}:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ (it commutes: $\iota_X^{-1}\circ\pi=\operatorname{Spec}\psi$) is cartesian: given a scheme $T$ and $a:T\to Z$, $b:T\to X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\psi\circ a=\iota_X^{-1}\circ b$, one has $b=\iota_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi\circ a=\pi\circ a$, so $a$ is the unique morphism $c:T\to Z$ with $\mathrm{id}_Z\circ c=a$ and $\pi\circ c=b$. Hence there is an isomorphism $Z\cong Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}X$ [def-pc-base-change] over $X$ carrying $\pi$ to the second projection, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ along $\iota_X^{-1}$, which is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a). Finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] is preserved by an isomorphism of sources over $X$: for an affine open $V\subseteq X$ the isomorphism identifies $\pi^{-1}(V)$ with the inverse image of $V$ under the projection (so it is affine) and the ring map $\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_Z(\pi^{-1}(V))$ with the corresponding ring map of the projection followed by a ring isomorphism (so it is finite). Thus $\pi$ is finite, and $Z$, $j$, $\pi$ are as required.
